issues.legal_issue: A remainder bequeathed after a life interest to the testator’s legal heirs vests at the testator’s death in the person who is then the sole legal heir, absent a contrary intention.
material_facts: The will gave the house to the testator’s wife for life and stated that after her death it would go to the testator’s legal heirs.
The son was the testator’s only legal heir when the testator died; the daughters became legal heirs under later succession law.
The will’s provision for the wife’s prior life interest did not indicate that vesting of the remainder was postponed.
issues.conclusion: The remainder vested in the son at the testator’s death and was not postponed until the wife’s death; the daughters did not take a share in the remainder under the will.
issues.legal_principle: Section 119 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925, including Illustration (iii), provides that a remainder ordinarily vests when the testator dies even if possession follows a prior life interest. The exception to Section 111 did not apply because the class was described by reference to the testator, not a specified individual other than the testator. Section 120 did not apply because the wife’s death was not a specified uncertain event. The Court relied on Chilanakuri Pullappa v. Guruka Bayanna, AIR 1962 AP 54, and P. Somasundaram v. K. Rajammal, AIR 1976 Mad 295, on Section 119; it distinguished N. Krishnammal v. R. Ekambram, (1979) 3 SCC 273, as involving a contingent bequest.

rule.if: will_construction_dispute and life_interest_precedes_remainder and remainder_given_to_testator_legal_heirs and sole_legal_heir_exists_at_testator_death

predicates.will_construction_dispute: The dispute requires the court to construe a will.
predicates.life_interest_precedes_remainder: The will gives one person a life interest before the remainder is to pass.
predicates.remainder_given_to_testator_legal_heirs: The will gives the remainder to the testator’s legal heirs.
predicates.sole_legal_heir_exists_at_testator_death: One person is the testator’s only legal heir when the testator dies.

issues.definition: When a will gives a life interest followed by a remainder to the testator’s legal heirs, and one person is the sole legal heir at the testator’s death, the remainder vests then in that person.

issues.legal_issue: A compromise resolving disputed claims to property may establish ownership according to its terms even when one party’s claimed interest arose under a will containing a restriction on transfer.
material_facts: The mother and son had competing claims to the house under different wills, and several suits between them were pending.
Their compromise declared the son owner of the properties in dispute, while giving the mother a right to reside in part of the house and maintenance.
The compromise was acted upon, and the mother did not challenge it during her lifetime.
issues.conclusion: The compromise was effective according to its terms: the son became owner of the house subject to the mother’s agreed right of residence and maintenance. It was a settlement of conflicting claims, not a transfer or surrender of the mother’s interest under the 1942 will.
issues.legal_principle: The compromise must be assessed in light of the disputed claims and circumstances existing when it was made. It resolved competing claims without deciding which will governed, and the restriction in the 1942 will did not invalidate that compromise. The rules requiring a total surrender of a widow’s estate did not apply because the mother’s interest was a life estate and the arrangement was a compromise, not a surrender.

predicates.family_property_dispute: The proceeding concerns disputed rights to family property.
predicates.competing_claims_are_pending: The parties have competing claims to the property in pending litigation.
predicates.compromise_resolves_claims_and_sets_out_: The parties make a compromise that resolves their claims and specifies their respective property rights.
predicates.compromise_is_not_challenged_or_shown_to: The compromise is not shown to have been involuntary or challenged by the party bound by it.

issues.definition: A compromise in a family property dispute is effective according to its terms when it resolves pending competing claims, specifies property rights, and is not shown to be involuntary or successfully challenged.

issues.legal_issue: A limited property interest given to a Hindu woman in recognition of a pre-existing right to maintenance becomes her absolute property when she retains a right to possession of that property.
material_facts: The compromise gave the mother a right to reside in the first floor of the house and maintenance, with a higher maintenance payment if she did not reside there.
The right of residence was given in recognition of her pre-existing right to maintenance.
She retained a right to possession of the first floor; the compromise had given the son rights over the rest of the house.
The mother did not give up her right to the first floor, and the evidence showed that she resided there before her death.
issues.conclusion: The mother became absolute owner of the first floor under Section 14(1) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, but did not become owner of the whole house.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(1) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, enlarges a Hindu woman’s limited interest into absolute ownership where the property is held in recognition of a pre-existing right. A right to possession need not amount to actual physical occupation. Section 14(1), rather than Section 14(2), applied because the right of residence was in recognition of the pre-existing right to maintenance. The Court relied on V. Tulasamma v. V. Sesha Reddi, (1977) 3 SCC 99, and Mangat Mal v. Punni Devi, (1995) 6 SCC 88.

predicates.female_hindu_has_limited_property_intere: A Hindu woman holds a limited interest in property.
predicates.interest_recognizes_preexisting_maintena: The interest was given in recognition of her pre-existing right to maintenance.
predicates.right_to_possession_is_retained: The woman retains a right to possession of the property.

issues.definition: A Hindu woman’s limited interest becomes absolute ownership when it recognizes her pre-existing maintenance right and she retains a right to possession.

issues.legal_issue: A party may rely on a statutory ground not specifically cited in the pleadings when the material facts supporting its application are pleaded and refusing to consider it would elevate a technicality over the applicable law.
material_facts: The pleadings repeatedly asserted that the claimant relied on rights through both parents, including the mother.
The facts needed to apply the statutory enlargement of the mother’s property interest were established in the case.
The opposing party’s objection was that the statute had not been specifically invoked earlier and that it had lacked an opportunity to contest its application.
issues.conclusion: The claimant could rely on Section 14 of the Hindu Succession Act despite not having specifically cited it in the pleadings or earlier proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: Order VI Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure governs pleadings, but pleadings need not cite the legal provision when the material facts are set out. A salutary statutory provision should not be denied effect on a technical pleading objection when the necessary facts are established. The Court relied on Kedar Lal Seal v. Hari Lal Seal, AIR 1952 SC 47, and applied the principle that Section 14 operates on its own force once its factual requirements are met.

rule.if: appeal_invokes_new_legal_ground and material_facts_supporting_ground_are_pleaded and necessary_facts_are_established and objection_is_only_technical_noncitation

predicates.appeal_invokes_new_legal_ground: A party invokes a legal ground in an appeal that was not specifically cited earlier.
predicates.material_facts_supporting_ground_are_ple: The pleadings state the material facts supporting the ground.
predicates.necessary_facts_are_established: The facts necessary for application of the ground are established in the proceeding.
predicates.objection_is_only_technical_noncitation: The objection is that the legal provision was not specifically cited, rather than that the supporting facts are absent.

issues.definition: A new legal ground may be considered on appeal when its supporting material facts were pleaded and established and the objection is only to the earlier omission of a specific citation.

issues.legal_issue: A limitation defence based on adverse possession fails when it was abandoned at an earlier appellate stage or when the party asserting it has not adequately pleaded when and how adverse possession began.
material_facts: The trial court found the suit within time, and the parties did not contest that finding in the intermediate appeal.
The defendants pleaded that adverse possession began in 1954, but that position depended on their unsuccessful claim under a later will.
They did not plead that adverse possession began under the compromise or at a later point, and the sale deed did not state that possession was delivered.
The mother retained and exercised her right to the first floor; the claimant brought the partition suit within the relevant limitation period and challenged the purchasers’ claimed rights.
issues.conclusion: The limitation defence was rejected. The defendants could not re-agitate the unchallenged finding that the suit was timely, and their adverse-possession plea was not sufficiently pleaded or established.
issues.legal_principle: A party cannot re-agitate a plea abandoned at an appellate stage. Adverse possession is a mixed question of fact and law, and the party asserting it must plead with sufficient clarity when the possession became adverse and the nature of that possession. A party asserting adverse possession has no equities in its favour and bears the burden of establishing the necessary facts.

predicates.partition_suit: The proceeding seeks partition or possession of property held in common.
predicates.limitation_finding_not_contested_in_inte: A finding that the suit is within time was not contested at an intermediate appellate stage.
predicates.adverse_possession_start_not_adequately_: The party asserting adverse possession has not clearly pleaded when and how that possession became adverse.
predicates.claimant_sued_within_limitation_period: The claimant brought the relevant claim within the applicable limitation period.

issues.definition: In a partition suit, a limitation defence is rejected if the timely-suit finding was not contested, the adverse-possession claim was inadequately pleaded, or the claimant sued within the limitation period.

issues.legal_issue: A purchaser under a conveyance executed by an authorized agent acquires only the interest held by the principal, and a sale of an entire property cannot transfer another owner’s distinct share.
material_facts: The son owned the ground floor under the compromise, while the mother became absolute owner of the first floor under Section 14(1).
After the mother’s death, her interest in the first floor devolved equally on her son and four daughters under Section 15 of the Hindu Succession Act.
The son’s general power of attorney executed a sale deed purporting to convey the whole house to the purchasers.
The son and his legal representatives did not challenge the sale deed.
issues.conclusion: The sale was valid and effective as to the ground floor. As to the first floor, the purchasers acquired only the son’s one-fifth share; the daughters retained their respective shares.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 14(1) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, the mother acquired absolute ownership of the first floor; under Section 15, that interest devolved on her son and four daughters in equal shares. A conveyance by an agent for the principal cannot transfer more than the principal owns. Because the principal’s side did not challenge the conveyance, it remained effective as to the principal’s own interest.

rule.if: property_transfer_dispute and authorized_agent_conveys_entire_property and principal_owns_only_part_of_property and principal_side_does_not_challenge_transfer

predicates.property_transfer_dispute: The proceeding concerns the extent of rights transferred by a conveyance.
predicates.authorized_agent_conveys_entire_property: An agent authorized by the principal executes a conveyance purporting to transfer the entire property.
predicates.principal_owns_only_part_of_property: The principal owns less than the entire property conveyed.
predicates.principal_side_does_not_challenge_transf: The principal and those representing the principal do not challenge the conveyance.

issues.definition: A transferee under a conveyance of an entire property acquires only the principal’s interest when the principal owns only part of it and does not challenge the transfer.
